rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ḥāqqah is the Hour in which the realities of deeds are established: believers' deeds and disbelievers' deeds alike become manifest and true.
rows.anchor: يعني الساعة التي فيها حقائق الأعمال، يقول يحق للمؤمنين عملهم، ويحق للكافرين عملهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question addressed to the Prophet magnifies the Hour because of its severity.
rows.anchor: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: { ومآ أدراك ما الحاقة } [آية: 3] تعظيما لها لشدتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He identifies the Hour as al-Qāriʿah, the event denied by Thamūd and ʿĀd, and notes its parallel in Sūrat al-Qāriʿah.
rows.anchor: ثم قال: هي القارعة، والساعة التي { كذبت } بها { ثمود وعاد بالقارعة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called al-Qāriʿah because God strikes His enemies with punishment.
rows.anchor: وإنما سميت القارعة لأن الله عز وجل يقرع أعداءه بالعذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He identifies wayl as a valley in Hell seventy years long, with immense nested branches and chambers containing fiery trees, worms, snakes, and scorpions.
rows.anchor: الويل واد في جهنم بعده مسيرة سبعين سنة، فيه تسعون ألف شعب، في كل شعب سبعون ألف شق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report about the pre-Islamic market says buyers received extra measure while sellers gave short measure, using two measures and two scales and shifting between them.
rows.anchor: وكان بسوق الجاهلية لهم كيلين وميزانين معلومة لا يعاب عليهم فيها

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When the Prophet arrived in Medina, he warned the traders about what they were doing.
rows.anchor: فلما قدم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة قال لهم: " ويل لكم مما تصنعون "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God confirmed the Prophet's warning by revealing the condemnation of those who shortmeasure.
rows.anchor: فأنزل الله تعالى التصديق على لسانه، فقال: { ويل للمطففين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He glosses their loss when measuring or weighing for others as giving them less than their due.
rows.anchor: فقال: { الذين إذا اكتالوا على الناس يستوفون وإذا كالوهم أو وزنوهم يخسرون } [آية: 3] يعني ينقصون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He warns that those who cheat in measure should consider whether they will be resurrected for a tremendous Day.
rows.anchor: ثم خوفهم فقال: { ألا يظن أولئك } الذين يفعلون هذا { أنهم مبعوثون ليوم عظيم } [آية: 5]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hāwiyah is the person's origin or abode: earth will not carry him, the sky will not shade him, and only the Fire remains; he compares this usage with umm al-qurā, the origin of towns, meaning Mecca.
rows.anchor: فذلك قوله: { فأمه هاوية } يعني أصله هاوية، كقوله: أم القرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says the blazing Fire heats six gates of Hell.
rows.anchor: يقول: نار حامية تحمى ستة أبواب من جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scales are light because of the person's evil deeds; truth is heavy and wholesome, whereas falsehood is light and vile.
rows.anchor: يقول: خفت موازينه بسيئاته وحق لميزان لا يقع فيه الحق أن يخف لأن الحق ثقيل مرىء، والباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about what the Fire is magnifies its severity.
rows.anchor: { ومآ أدراك ما هيه } تعظيما لشدتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He describes the Fire as burning at its utmost heat.
rows.anchor: هي: { نار حامية } يقول: انتهى حرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamzah is the slanderer who backbites a man behind his back when he is absent.
rows.anchor: يعني الطعان المغتاب الذي إذا غاب عنه الرجل اغتابه من خلفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lumazah is the overbearing person who acts tyrannically toward someone to his face.
rows.anchor: يعني الطاغى إذا رآه طغى عليه في وجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says the opening condemnation was revealed about al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah al-Makhzūmī.
rows.anchor: نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومى، ثم نعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man gathered and prepared wealth to buy servants and livestock.
rows.anchor: يقول: الذي استعد مالا ليشترى به الخدم والحيوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He imagines his wealth will preserve him from death until the wealth itself is spent.
rows.anchor: من الموت، فلا يموت حتى يفنى ماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rejects this belief: neither his wealth nor his children will make him immortal.
rows.anchor: يقول الله عز وجل { كلا } لا يخلده ماله وولده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He will be cast into the Crusher; the question about the Crusher magnifies its severity, since it crushes bones and eats flesh until it reaches the heart.
rows.anchor: يقول: ليتركن في الحطمة { ومآ أدراك ما الحطمة } [آية: 5] تعظيما لشدتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fire of God remains kindled for its inhabitants and never goes out.
rows.anchor: ثم أخبر عنها، فقال: { نار الله الموقدة } [آية: 6] على أهلها لا تخمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fire eats flesh and skin until its heat reaches the hearts, then new flesh is given and consumed again to the former state.
rows.anchor: تأكل اللحم والجلود حتى يخلص حرها إلى القلوب، ثم تكسى لحما جديدا، ثم تقبل عليه وتأكله حتى يصير إلى منزلته الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muṣadah means shut or covered: the doors are sealed and secured with fiery iron stakes, so no door opens, relief enters, or anguish leaves forever.
rows.anchor: { إنها عليهم مؤصدة } [آية: 8] يعني مطبقة { في عمد ممددة } [آية: 9] يقول: طبقت الأبواب ثم شدت بأوتاد من حديد من نار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In an alternative explanation, hamzah is a talebearer who carries speech between people.
rows.anchor: فأما الهمزة فالذي ينم الكلام إلى الناس وهو النمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the same alternative explanation, lumazah is one who gives a man a nickname he dislikes; Muqātil identifies him as al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah.
rows.anchor: وأما اللمزة، فهو الذي يلقب الرجل بما يكره، وهو الوليد بن المغيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He characterizes al-Walīd as a gossiper who gave people nicknames arrogantly and mocked them.
rows.anchor: كان رجلا نماما، وكان يلقب الناس من التجبر والعظمة، وكان يستهزىء بالناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqātil links the condemnation to the description of the man in 74:11–12 and says he owned gardens in Mecca and Taif whose bounty continued in both winter and summer.
rows.anchor: وكان له حديقتان، حديقة بمكة، وحديقة بالطائف، كان لا ينقطع خيره شتاء ولا صيفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He glosses the phrase about present sons as heads of households and says al-Walīd had seven sons.
rows.anchor: يعني أرباب البيوت، وكان له سبعة بنين، قال: ومهدت له تمهيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God had fully expanded the man's wealth; he still hoped for more, but God calls him obstinate toward the signs.
rows.anchor: بسطت له في المال كل البسط، ثم يطمع أن أزيد كلا إنه كان لآياتنا عنيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative says the man swore he could distribute his wealth throughout Quraysh while alive without exhausting it, and challenged the threat of poverty.
rows.anchor: قسم مالى يمينا وشمالا على قريش ما دمت حيا ما فنى، فكيف تعدنى الفقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He is told that the One who gave him his wealth can take it away; this affects him, and he begins counting his possessions.
rows.anchor: إن الذي أعطاك، قادر على أن يأخذه منك، فوقع في قلبه من ذلك شىء، ثم عمد إلى ماله فعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He counts and inventories his gold, silver, land, gardens, and slaves.
rows.anchor: ما كان ذهب أو فضة، أو أرض، أو حديقة، أو رقيق، فعده وأحصاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He tells Muhammad that even if all his counted wealth were bread it would not run out, and the condemnation in Sūrat al-Humazah is revealed in response.
rows.anchor: يا محمد تعدنى الفقر والله لو كان هذا خبزا ما فنى، فأنزل الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He repeats that the man's wealth will not make him immortal.
rows.anchor: كلا } لا يخلده، ثم استأنف، فقال: { لينبذن في الحطمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about the Crusher is an intensification of its severity.
rows.anchor: فقال: { لينبذن في الحطمة ومآ أدراك ما الحطمة } تعظيما لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a wretched person enters Hell, an angel takes him around its gates and forms of torment, then opens the gate of the Crusher, which is one of Hell's gates.
rows.anchor: طاف به الملك في أبوابها في ألوان العذاب وفتح له باب الحطمة،وهى باب من أبواب جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Crusher's fire is so intense that it consumes other fire and has never gone out since God created it.
rows.anchor: وهي نار تأكل النار من شدة حرها، وما خمدت من يوم خلقها الله عز وجل إلى يوم يدخلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the gate opens, fire burns the skin, flesh, sinews, and bones, but not the heart or eye, which are the faculties of understanding and sight.
rows.anchor: فتحرق الجلد واللحم والعصب والعظم ولا تحرق القلب ولا العين، وهو ما يعقل به ويبصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He quotes the verse about death approaching from every direction: every hair's place is reached by death, though the person is not dead.
rows.anchor: ثم تلا: ويأتيه الموت من كل مكان، وما هو بميت، يقول: ليس في جسده موضع شعرة إلا والموت يأتيه من ذلك المكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When monotheists leave through Hell's upper gate, the inhabitants of the seven gates, described as the lowest level, remain inside.
rows.anchor: إذا خرج الموحدون من الباب الأعلى، وهي جهنم، قال أهل تلك السبعة الأبواب، وهي أسفل درك من النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask the people of the sixth gate what brought them into Saqar; those people answer that they did not pray or feed the poor.
rows.anchor: لأهل الباب السادس: ما سلككم في سقر يقول: ما أدخلكم في سقر، قالوا لم نك من المصلين ولم نك نطعم المسكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inmates try grieving and then screaming for ages, but neither helps them.
rows.anchor: ثم يقولون: تعالوا حتى نجزع، فيجزعون حقبا من الدهر فلا ينفعهم شيئا، ثم يقولون: تعالوا حتى نصرخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They then decide to be patient and silent in hope of mercy, but after ages this also brings them no benefit.
rows.anchor: فلعل الله عز وجل إذا صبرنا وسكتنا أن يرحمنا، فيصبرون حقبا من الدهر، فلا يغني عنهم شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inmates conclude that grieving or enduring makes no difference and they have no escape.
rows.anchor: سوآء علينآ أجزعنآ أم صبرنا ما لنا من محيص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They cry out to be taken from Hell, promising that if they return to wrongdoing they will be unjust.
rows.anchor: ثم ينادون: أخرجنا منها فإن عدنا فإنا ظالمون

rows.speaker: الله عز وجل
rows.claim: The Lord of Might answers them from above the Throne by ordering them to remain there and speak no more.
rows.anchor: ينادي رب العزة من فوق العرش: اخسئوا فيها ولا تكلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their ears are deafened, their hearts sealed, and the gates closed and fastened shut against one another.
rows.anchor: فتصم آذانهم ويختم على قلوبهم، وتغلق عليهم أبوابها، فيطبق كل واحد على صاحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gates are secured by iron nails of fire as large as mountains; no breath enters and the heat of the Fire cannot escape.
rows.anchor: بمسامير من حديد من نار كأمثال الجبال، فلا يلج فيها روح، ولا يخرج منها حر النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They eat from the Fire and hear only groaning and gasping; Muqātil prays for protection from it through God's bounty, generosity, and mercy.
rows.anchor: ويأكلون من النار، ولا يسمع فيها إلا الزفير والشهيق، نسأل الله المعافاة منها بفضله وجوده، ورحمته
